The oscillations in diverse systems, from biological to physical phenomena, are widespread and have been extensively studied over recent years. This research focuses on an array of non-identical oscillators that exhibit a uniformly distributed hump in their characteristics, allowing for multiple stable states, including solitary and paired occurrences within a phase-locked configuration. Our results reveal two key features in these systems: locally, the phase coupling tends to be weaker and exhibits a similar pattern for all pairs of oscillators, regardless of their specific parameters; while globally, the phase coupling for all oscillators can either become synchronized or remain desynchronized, depending on a boundary condition that encompasses the entire parameter space of the system. This study provides valuable insights into understanding complex dynamics in biological and mechanical systems.

The well-established Aldous--Broder and Wilson algorithms generate uniform spanning trees through random walks. Specifically, Wilson's algorithm constructs a uniform spanning tree by randomly extending it one vertex at a time, whereas the Aldous--Broder algorithm extends the tree one step at a time as an ongoing process. By examining the tree generated by Wilson's algorithm at any given point in time, our analysis reveals that it matches the tree produced by Aldous--Broder after the same number of iterations. This reveals that at any given point in time, Wilson's algorithm operates under a two-phase framework: an initial exploration phase that discovers new tree components, and an attachment phase that connects existing components.

A comprehensive dataset called MusicTM-Dataset has been created to integrate sheet music, lyrics, and audio recordings. By combining these elements, the dataset enables synchronization of musical features and a deeper understanding of music through a unified representation. Developed for advanced music tasks like automatic score transcription, this dataset will contribute to the growth of multimodal music AI by promoting innovative research through a robust benchmark.

Modern language models like word2vec, used since 2009, can capture the relationships between words in a mathematical space where similar words are placed closer together.
This concept has been applied in various fields, including generating fictional stories with thematic consistency and analyzing political biases in news headlines.
To further utilize this capability, we propose a method that combines solid knowledge bases with soft linguistic models to provide both and utilize one to enhance the other.
By combining a graph-based tool Ontodia with the distributed representations from word2vec, we enhance examination of textual information by providing suggestions for related entities based on text proximity.
We then apply this enhanced method to analyze data within the Wikidata knowledge base, which includes the knowledge of who painted which artwork, in order to propose related entities such as other paintings or artists.

The influence of intensity-dependent dispersion on dark soliton stability in 1D and 2-photon absorption systems is investigated. Numerical solutions of the nonlinear Schrödinger equation are used to model dark soliton behavior. Research reveals that ignoring absorption effects in optical systems is not advisable, as 1-photon absorption mitigates and enhances nonlinearity, whereas 2-photon absorption exacerbates and consequently 1- and 2-photon absorption have opposing impacts on soliton stability.

We present a novel framework, called a lot, which offers users flexible and adaptable support during the exploration of visual data. Lots allow for the creation of dynamic workflows that link user actions in an application to provided assistance through explanations and recommendations. The framework's capabilities are demonstrated in a prototype system with a comprehensive set of lots on financial data, resulting in a user experience that combines the benefits of specialized visual analytics tools with the adaptability of the lot-based approach. The proposed framework's potential applications and uses are thoroughly examined.

Optimally designed magnetic fields within the stellarator require precise placement of specially shaped coils to create optimal plasma conditions. In contrast, more conventional coil designs magnetic fields deviate significantly from optimal requirements, necessitating correction through carefully positioned coils with adjustable strengths and positions. These corrective coils should ideally integrate seamlessly into the stellarator's main coil set to minimize overall size, complexity, and cost. Utilizing a specialized optimization method called optimal parameter matching, researchers are able to efficiently determine the required corrections for multiple coil sets, showcasing the feasibility of effective current distribution and position arrangements. Through simulations, the proposed corrections successfully reduce the stellarator's internal magnetic field imperfections, demonstrating improved plasma stability, and suitable shapes for its internal surfaces.

A new approach utilizing magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) in conjunction with a chemical exchange saturation transfer (CEST) technique has successfully demonstrated the capability to monitor heat distribution within a gas-solid bed. An 8-inch diameter MRI scanner was used to detect the temperature in a solid-liquid stationary bed, with a custom-built CEST probe and electron-donating molecules enabling the non-invasive measurement of temperatures up to 80°C. The MRI scanner provided a spatial resolution of approximately 1 cm, with a 6°C temperature resolution. By combining magnetic fields to encode spatial information, a 3D map of the bed's temperature distribution can be generated. This research showcases the potential for MRI-CEST to study complex solid-liquid systems in the presence of high temperatures.

Using a computational model, the behavior of two distinct cellular components
was investigated in detail through advanced simulations. The results revealed that
the components form a complex pattern when mixed together in the same environment.
This pattern is characterized by the formation of dense clusters of the components
at specific locations, interspersed with less dense, homogenous areas. The
component that forms the framework for one of the structures in the mixture plays
a crucial role in determining its overall shape and structure, particularly when
it has irregular, uneven surfaces. This phenomenon has been observed in real-life
examples, such as the interaction between proteins and DNA molecules.

In the context of solar physics, we delve into the dynamics of solar eruptions, focusing on the leading and trailing spots within the leading polarity region of an X-class flare eruption on July 23rd of 2012. Utilizing data from the Helioseismic and Magnetic Imager on the Solar Dynamics Observatory, we've observed the rotational motion of a active region situated at the photosphere, located near the equator with a longitudinal angle of 30 degrees. As the active region rotated, it underwent a significant disturbance, resulting in a coronal mass ejection accompanied by a solar flare. This study is the first to document the role of active region rotation in triggering both a coronal mass ejection and a solar flare.

The core assumption of the motivic b-filtered topological Mumford conjecture is that the space of marked Riemann surfaces has a specific topological structure, which can be described as being equivalent to the free category of freely generated elements. This assumption has already been validated in nearly all instances, except for a specific exception that was resolved recently. A new, more intricate topological Mumford conjecture arises from an alternative hypothesis - the assertion that certain complex cohomology spaces are motivated. The verification of such a hypothesis implies the validity of the core assumption. We explore this motivation assertion for the moduli space of hyperbolic surfaces, which differs from the core assumption in its consideration of a different set of geometric features, focused on shears rather than rotation. This alternative hypothesis has been verified for certain surface types and was verified for another key surface type just a few months ago.

This research investigates an comparison of multilevel preconditioners for solving linear systems in computational cardiac mechanics. Three types of preconditioners were compared: classic algebraic hierarchical preconditioners (AHPC), standard physics-based smoothed finite element method (SOFESM), and a new hybrid version combining both methods (AHPSOFESM). A significant limitation of cardiac mechanics models is the size of simulated systems, which can reach up to 10 million degrees of freedom, rendering direct solution methods impractical and making iterative solvers with effective preconditioning essential for model accuracy and efficiency. By blending algebraic and physics-based techniques, the hybrid preconditioner exhibits superior performance. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of AHPSOFESM in significantly reducing iteration counts and computational time when solving systems as large as 10 million unknowns on clusters of 32 processors.

The growing significance of user-generated content systems enabled by tagging techniques has sparked considerable interest in the potential of tag-based systems to offer collaborative tag management, akin to co-browsing. Tagging content collectively not only influences system performance but also reflects collaborative user behavior. Tagging systems, such as Del.icio.us, Flickr, and LinkedInfluence, have shown varying levels of success, but currently lack effective tools for harnessing user-generated content to facilitate browsing and tag management. To address this, we conducted an empirical study on a social tagging system to gain insights into tag usage, interest sharing, and cooperative user behavior. The resulting data analysis informed the development of tag-based system features, which we implemented and evaluated user responses to. The study and its findings provide a foundation for further research, while also serving as a model for similar co-browsing systems.

A novel type of anisotropic acoustic metamaterial, the microacoustic metagrating, has been successfully developed using advanced 3D printing technology. This innovative structure exhibits enhanced acoustic properties and holds great potential for applications in ultrasonic imaging and manipulation. Thanks to two technologies, printing within a great depth range in water and simultaneous phase and amplitude control of the ultrasonic beam, the application fields of this metamaterial have been greatly expanded. These capabilities allow for the exploration and development of new uses for this microacoustic metagrating in ultrasonic imaging and manipulation.

We investigate the interplay between the 2-D compressible FENE dumbbell model and the 2-D compressible Navier-Stokes/FENE dumbbell model, demonstrating that the long-term behavior of the model's global strong solutions can be significantly influenced by initial conditions when transitioning from a Navier slip to a no-slip boundary. Furthermore, we establish that the solution to the no-slip boundary scenario can cross over and remain superior to that of the slip boundary, an outcome that diverges from the findings of recent theoretical work on compressible Navier-Stokes/Goldstein-Kinoshita-Cracknell dumbbell models.

Integrating Integrated Access and Backhaul in 5G networks via wireless backhaul can significantly improve 5G network performance and efficiency by reducing infrastructure costs, enhancing flexibility, and increasing deployment speed. The Non-terrestrial Network's use of satellite technology addresses some Non-terrestrial Network challenges, yet it fails to address all Mobile IAB (Integrated Access and Backhaul) obstacles. A comprehensive paper titled "Mobile IAB: Issues, Solutions and Obstacles" provides an in-depth analysis of Mobile IAB's unique requirements and constraints, distinguishing it from other NTN use cases. The paper also identifies and examines various engineering challenges and proposes potential solutions for each.

In this study, we conduct an evidence-based analysis of five key hyperparameters in evolutionary algorithms (EA) using five distinct global sensitivity analysis methods. The investigation focuses on EA hyperparameter effects across five different optimization problems, both continuous and discrete. The results highlight that an excessive mutation rate significantly harms discrete EAs, whereas poor selection methods have minimal impact on discrete EAs, but significantly affect continuous EAs. Furthermore, we find that EA robustness to certain hyperparameter adjustments can be exploited to facilitate more efficient tuning. The findings support a new, hyperparameter effect-informed approach to EA tuning, which is detailed in associated research.

In one-dimensional quantum mechanics, our investigation centers on the time-dependent wave function u=u(t,x), which satisfies the time-dependent Schrödinger equation: -d^2u/dt/dt = -1/2 d^2u/dx/dx + V(x)u. We initially established the equivalence between global existence and global positivity. Furthermore, according to our recent findings in arXiv:2101.00183, which used semigroup theory, we were able to expand our knowledge on the behavior of the wave equation in both time and space. However, due to the equation's nonlinearity, its solutions do not generally maintain smoothness for all time, even with smooth initial conditions. To address this issue, we introduced two new concepts for initial conditions: condition A, which ensures a smooth, global solution, and condition B, which also guarantees a smooth, global solution but comes with additional technical complexities. Our examination of the behavior of the wave equation in both time and space, along with the conditions A and B, has led to several surprising findings. For instance, although a global solution may exist, it may not decay to zero as time approaches infinity. Similarly, although the condition B implies a smooth solution, it does not necessarily imply the absence of singularities in the first time derivative. To maintain consistency, we also redefined the condition B to not include the decay requirement.

Over recent years, significant advancements in reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms have been noted, yet their practical deployment in real-world applications remains a considerable hurdle. Multiple evaluation frameworks exist to accelerate the development of new RL algorithms, yet existing solutions are hindered by a lack of support for continuous action spaces, rendering a comprehensive assessment of current RL algorithms challenging. To address this limitation, we have developed L2Explorer, an advanced evaluation framework designed specifically for support of continuous action spaces. Distinguishing itself from traditional evaluation frameworks, L2Explorer offers an innovative approach through its support for eternal reinforcement learning. By enabling eternal reinforcement learning, users can now investigate how RL algorithms perform in infinite action support scenarios. As a result, we have successfully evaluated 33 state-of-the-art RL algorithms across 21 tasks, evaluating their actual utility. The findings reveal notable differences among these algorithms in terms of their eternal reward levels, rendering their comparisons more meaningful. The code for our framework can be accessed through the following link: https://github.com/l2explorer/L2Explorer.

The Large Integral Field at a Extremely large Telescope (LIGER) prototype is a small-volume device composed of a 30x30 pixel grid of 1.5 cm slabs filled with Dopant-saturated Dopant-sense Doped Semiconductor Optical Detector arrays, paired with a custom-designed optical system featuring a 0.5 m focal length. This setup captures 100 spatial resolution levels across a 10 deg. field of view, while 0.7 micrometer DODSAs record the full integral field spectral spectrum. Currently, LIGER is operational at the William Ogawa Metrology Lab at Keck Observatory in Hawaii, where initial tests have captured 8 hours of data. The collected data requires post-processing in multiple stages, beginning with removing background noise, followed by removing any remaining background, and finally, normalizing the spectra. The software framework responsible for these operations is designed to be modular and adaptable to various applications, such as exoplanet detection and galaxy formation studies. In addition to its versatility, the framework is paired with a hardware-based trigger system to synchronize data capture with LIGER's imaging cycles. As a result, the LIGER camera has successfully captured its first dataset at the Keck Observatory, marking a significant milestone in the development of this cutting-edge technology.

This study focuses on the 2D incompressible Navier-Stokes equations, revealing the long-term, spatially decaying asymptotic behavior of solutions near Couette flow type traveling waves, which correspond to shearing flows at various speeds in the boundary.

Our research focuses on controlling the linear polarization of exciton-polariton condensates using only optical means, which is largely unknown. Firstly, we demonstrate that in an unpumped state following a laser pulse, the polarization changes based on the pulse's polarization, occurring in a spin-dependent timeframe. This effect is a consequence of the spin-orbit coupling between the polarization and the movement of the polariton, which is controlled by the polarization of the laser. Additionally, our research shows that in low-pumped conditions, the polarization stabilization time is polarization-sensitive in single polariton systems, but not in exciton-polariton condensates. Furthermore, our research reveals that in coupled polariton condensates within a spin-filter structure, the polarization management varies significantly, which is also influenced by the polarization of the pump laser. This research provides valuable insights into the polarization manipulation of light-matter systems at full-speed, which is crucial for developing complex photonic devices that can be controlled with precision.

This study starts with nonlocal deterministic equations that include a nonlinearity similar to Kardar-Parisi-Zhang equations but with a nonlocal "slope term." We find that these equations yield a corresponding stochastic equation by adding white noise to the "slope term," which we then use to prove existence and uniqueness of weak solutions to the stochastic equation. This existence of weak solutions is then used to prove the presence of a Markovian random field of heights, which is used to establish strong well-posedness of the deterministic equation.

COVID-19 has spread worldwide, prompting concerns about the potential for uncontrolled transmission in numerous countries, including South Africa. In the absence of effective treatments and vaccines, nations have relied on heuristics and real-time data to inform their public health policies. Essential metrics for tracking the pandemic in South Africa include confirmed cases and deaths, though these figures are believed to significantly underrepresent the true extent of the issue. To address this disparity, our research presents a theoretical model of the underlying dynamics of unreported cases and deaths in the context of COVID-19 in South Africa. By analyzing reported data on confirmed cases and deaths, our model provides estimates of the true number of cases and deaths as well as the underlying infection rate. These estimates are then utilized to forecast future deaths. Furthermore, our analysis suggests that relying on past mortality rates to forecast the future is less accurate than a forecasting model that takes into account changing testing policies. These insights provide valuable insights that can be applied to the broader monitoring of infectious diseases.

Freiman's 3k-4 conjecture posited that any subset A of integers with n elements and less than n elements squared would have a size of at least n elements plus the size of a difference between pairs of elements in A. We have demonstrated that if the size of this subset A satisfies three conditions, then the first inequality holds: the subset must contain less than n elements squared, the subset must contain less than half the pairs of elements in A that are unique, and the subset must contain more than half the unique pairs of elements in A. These conditions enhance previously established enhancements to Freiman's 3k-4 conjecture.

A comprehensive dataset of 10,000 images has been compiled for the purpose of detecting diabetic retinopathy and cup-disc ratio determination. The combined collection of back-projection retinal images and optical coherence tomography contains various phases affected by diabetic retinopathy, spanning from mild to severe. The unified images enable the direct comparison of disease progression between different phases. This unified dataset is utilized in training a deep learning model that integrates visual features from a single image and a small multi-modal image context to produce classification outcomes. The proposed method demonstrates enhanced performance in categorizing diabetic retinopathy and tomography with areas under the receiver operating characteristic curves of 0.950 and 0.930 respectively.

Researchers have been investigating the potential of using machine learning to predict ICU admission requirements and disease progression in COVID-19 patients. The team aimed to explore the characteristics that could aid in predicting ICU admission needs, utilizing the public Xray5k dataset. The dataset was analyzed to create subgroups based on radiological severity, and these groups were compared using the ImageCLEF evaluation criteria. The study revealed distinct texture patterns in patients who did not require ICU admission versus those with severe conditions. The groups showed little overlap in terms of texture, and these findings align with existing literature suggesting that COVID-19 severity is influenced by factors such as tissue damage and inflammation. The study's results indicate that texture analysis could be a valuable tool in predicting ICU admission needs and disease progression in patients.

A substantial body of research has explored the transmission eigenvalue problem within uniform spherical media. A particular interest lies in identifying media boundaries through given transmission eigenfunctions. A mathematical approach is proposed to necessary determine media boundaries from directly measured transmission eigenfunctions without needing to perform inverse problems commonly associated with determining eigenfunctions from media parameters. Moreover, a relationship between original and transformed media is demonstrated when a transmission eigenfunction exhibits a specific transmission zero.

Identifying user intent in conversations is a crucial step in processing language, but current methods are heavily reliant on feature engineering and struggle with accuracy, especially for smaller datasets. This research builds upon previous work on user intent detection by incorporating pre-training with language models like BERT and introducing comparative learning to enhance feature extraction. The proposed enhancements result in a more robust and accurate user intent detection system, with the main contributions being the integration of pre-trained models and the development of a novel extraction method, which has demonstrated superior performance in multiple experiments and achieved a remarkable 92.8% accuracy on a complex dataset.

Global sections of a simplicial sheaf form a sheaf, specifically a simplicial object in the category of sheaves, which enables a more efficient and transparent approach to defining and working with global objects in the associated hypercovering theory that controls simplicial objects with sheaf-like properties.

In the study of finite groups, researchers have established an upper limit on the number of subgroups within certain types of groups, specifically those with cyclic normal subgroups and specific index ranges. Specifically, for groups where the sum of the sizes of these subgroups and the index is greater than or equal to nine, an upper limit on the total count of subgroups has been found. This limit grows at a rate no faster than $p^6$ for the $p$-part of the group's order. Also, above the value of nine, this upper limit is achieved by symmetric groups. As previously introduced by Ashok and Shu, these results lead to an upper limit on the count of subgroups within finite nilpotent groups based on their order. This limit no longer outpaces $f(n)=n(\log n)^{6-\epsilon}$ for any positive value of $\epsilon$ as previously thought.

The Automatic Balanced Scaled (ABS) H2 formula has become the go-to solution for stabilizing and achieving second-order performance in continuous and discrete systems. Over the years, numerous alternative methods have been proposed to replace it, yet each comes with significant drawbacks. Due to its widespread success and numerous applications in engineering fields, a comprehensive review of the ABS H2 formula from various perspectives is long overdue.

Although significant advancements have been made in object recognition, 
accurely detecting associations between semantic categories such as a painting 
and its artist, remains challenging due to the diverse visual styles. Current 
methods relying on mutual information and attention mechanisms often fail, as 
they mistakenly identify non-associated categories as being related. To address 
this issue, we introduce a novel approach to Visual Association Detection that 
consists of two key components. Firstly, we introduce a structured graph that 
captures the inherent semantic connections between words, and extract feature 
embeddings from a pre-trained language model. These embeddings are then used to 
refine the initial association detection results. Secondly, we introduce a novel 
error-filtering module that eliminates false positives by combining graph 
embeddings with a multi-layer perceptron trained to minimize detection errors. 
Experimental results on a publicly available dataset demonstrate the proposed 
method's superiority, achieving an improvement in mean average precision of 10.4% 
over the existing state-of-the-art solutions.

The cost of quantum association in the context of Fock state measurements has been established as a fundamental concept.  By examining the minimal energy required for extracting information about a quantum state from a feeble measurement, we've found that this cost is directly related to the square of the state's photon wavefunction at zero, i.e., $\psi(0)^2$.  This finding has significant implications, as it reveals the cost to be substantially lower than previously thought under minimum disturbance measurements, particularly when the quantum state contains a non-zero amplitude at zero.  Furthermore, we've identified a class of Fock states, characterized by a negative amplitude at zero and a rapidly decaying tail, in which the association cost is nearly equivalent to the average photon number, $\bar{n}$.  These statements constitute previously elusive minimum cost theorems, providing a framework for optimizing quantum association in various applications, including the design of robust quantum communication protocols and the development of efficient quantum error correction schemes.

This research focuses on a previously overlooked task in social network analysis: relationship graph prediction. The predicted relationships can enhance tasks like identifying connections between people, determining contacts, and mapping social networks. A proposed approach uses existing relationship data from a graph of interconnected individuals to predict new, unseen relationships between a group of individuals. The proposed method is based on a deep learning technique that creates a comprehensive graph of interconnected individuals using various features like demographic information, and then uses a deep learning-based graph neural network to predict the relationship type between two individuals. The proposed approach was tested on two publicly available datasets, demonstrating better performance compared to existing methods.

Recent breakthroughs in object recognition using deep neural networks have led to the development of a new task called visual object identification. This object identification task shares similarities with sentence identification, but current methods struggle with generalizing novel semantic concepts. To address this issue, a new framework called the dynamic graph message transmission network has been proposed to learn visual concepts by leveraging the dynamic interaction between visual and textual data. In our framework, the conceptual relationships between words are represented in a semantic graph, whose nodes represent existing knowledge that informs the visual graph's structure. This results in a dual-graph representation where the interaction between the two graphs produces new insights for learning. Moreover, a graph attention mechanism is employed to regulate the flow of information and generate final predictions. Empirical results demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework across multiple visual object identification tasks, yielding competitive results in popular benchmark datasets.

This paper explores the design of digital constant multiplication units, focusing on an efficient method for multiplying by numbers like 0xA and 0xB. By utilizing shift, add, and save operations in place of traditional addition, the proposed algorithm significantly reduces the required hardware. A universal method is also proposed to create efficient multipliers for any 32-bit number, ultimately leading to a new structure for partial products that allows for faster processing and simpler circuitry.

The growing interest in quantum computing is largely driven by its potential to efficiently solve complex mathematical problems, such as the hidden subgroup problem, which underlies key quantum algorithms.  In contrast to classical computing, where the primary focus has been on increasing processing power, quantum computing offers a unique opportunity to leverage fundamental physical properties for solving certain types of problems more effectively.  This paper explores the emerging field of quantum machine learning and reviews recent breakthroughs in quantum neural network research.  It also discusses the practical challenges associated with large-scale quantum computing and outlines research hurdles that need to be overcome for the successful application of quantum computing in solving complex machine learning tasks.

Radiation reaction from electromagnetic fields causes particles to lose energy, an effect that can be utilized to increase the energy of a circular beam. A Radio Frequency Booster, using this principle, enhances the beam's energy by a factor of $1+\Delta E/E_0$. Research into RF Boosters as an option for increasing the energy of existing facilities led to exploration of various technologies at work function reduced cathodes, optical cavities, and advanced particle acceleration methods. This research resulted in a successful demonstration, capable of a $100\times$ energy multiplier, which serves as a basis for future developments. These include implementing new RF Booster technologies on facilities of different energy scales, ranging from low-energy tables-top systems to high-energy colliders, which could potentially provide up to four orders of magnitude increase in energy range.

In the search for precision testing of physics beyond the standard model, building a muon collider is considered a promising option. This project faces two main challenges: creating a reliable muon source and developing effective muon storage and acceleration techniques due to rapid muon decays. A review of various proposals for muon collider projects reveals the progress made so far, but also highlights the technical difficulties and hurdles that remain to be overcome.

A relativistic viscous fluid's equilibrium states can be described by a specific equation involving density, temperature, and flow velocity. These equilibrium conditions stem from both energy and momentum conservation principles. When disturbed from equilibrium, the changes in fluid variables obey a set of linear equations. These equations can be factored into a product of two operators, one related to momentum and the other to time derivatives and fluid velocity changes. Setting the disturbance as a function of time and space, the resulting expression can be simplified into a quadratic equation in terms of the wave number and flow velocity. This equation can be solved for the angular frequency, yielding two solutions corresponding to different physical modes.

Our research investigates the potential for detecting low-mass primordial black holes (PBHs) with masses ranging from $10^{14}$ to $10^{17}$ grams through their impact on polarized photons and electrons near the Earth. These PBHs would emit a steady stream of gamma rays as they evaporate, which could be obstructed by the Earth's magnetic field, leading to a background of charged particles that evaporating PBHs could be detected in gamma-ray experiments observing the sky away from the Earth. We discovered that a new window of low-energy gamma rays, detectable by the upcoming CTA, may be opened by the charged particles of the PBHs, which could potentially be mistaken for signals from magnetars.

A novel four-stage pipeline processor has been created to demonstrate the practical application of Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE), specifically using the TFHE scheme, which enables computations on encrypted data without requiring decryption. Our proposed virtual safe instruction set architecture consists of basic instructions designed to work efficiently within a limited gate budget and small bootstrapping circuits of TFHE. Each stage of our processor executes a simplified, single-threaded instruction sequence. Although our design has a lower performance compared to circuit-based FHE implementations, it offers significant advantages in terms of development time, storage requirements, and bandwidth when dealing with large applications. Moreover, our implementation can be easily extended to support RNS and DFS schemes.

We have developed a polynomial-time approximation scheme (PTAS) for solving specific types of combinatorial optimization problems on unweighted hypergraphs with limited edges per vertex in their interaction matrix. The approach involves adapting a previously proposed heuristic framework for similar problems on sparse graphs, specifically those editable in $o(\log n)/\log \log n$ degrees. By carefully analyzing the effects of edge density and applying structural results from related work, we successfully extend the applicability of the PTAS to instances with polylogarithmic edges. The final approach combines these insights into a simplified analysis and an efficient PTAS running time, outperforming earlier solutions.

Despite widespread adoption in various applications, few comprehensive studies delve into the behavior of pre-trained language models when used without supervision, unlike supervised methods that require extensive annotations. To better understand this, we conduct an in-depth investigation of popular pre-trained models on small datasets, examining their performance, the types of tasks they can accomplish, and their limitations compared to supervised models. To provide context, we also consider the effects of increased dataset size and explore ways to enhance the pre-trained models' abilities. Our research sheds light on the capabilities of these models in small-data settings, offering insights for future pre-trained model development and research directions.

A novel weakly-supervised approach for semantic segmentation in RGB images is proposed, leveraging a pre-trained hyperspectral imaging model. This method utilizes a single hSIF hyper-point in conjunction with the corresponding label set from HSI to achieve cityscape scene segmentation in RGB images. By exploiting pre-existing HSI data, the proposed technique bypasses the need for extensive RGB image datasets for training. Moreover, it extends the applicability of semantic segmentation to scenarios where hyperspectral imaging is feasible, despite the significantly higher spectral resolution. Thorough experiments on a real-world dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed weakly-supervised method, which outperforms comparable approaches in various evaluations.

Recently, a new class of ultra-short period pulsating planets has been discovered. These planets, characterized by their extremely short orbital periods, often possess distorted star shapes due to their close proximity. The research focuses on a particular pair of these planets orbiting the star HD 181086, which displays unique, changing amplitude and phase patterns. The variability in the star's pulsations is likely a result of its distorted shape, which is thought to be caused by two large "manacles" or star deformations. The irregular fluctuations in the star's pulsations are believed to be a sign of these manacles changing their shape over time. The research suggests that one of these star deformations might be in the process of spinning faster, which could be attributed to interactions with the inner planet. This interaction could trigger a chain of events that ultimately affect the star's pulsations. The findings highlight the complex relationships between planets and their host stars, and their impact on stellar behavior.

We analyze a new problem in theoretical computer science, where we seek to create functions that map binary inputs to single-bit outputs by manipulating individual bits. The functions we consider are built from basic operations including bitwise AND, OR, and NOT, as well as XOR and STXOR. The critical aspect is that these operations can be executed in constant time within a specific model of computation, and our goal is to understand which more complex mappings can be achieved with these building blocks. The key findings are as follows:

First, it's proven that any function taking n boolean inputs and producing m bits of output, where the size of the mapping is k, can be realized using O(k) basic operations. The large OR, AND, and STXOR components are essential, and even with limited access to these, it's possible to solve 2-SAT efficiently, and with zero access to these components, it's still possible to solve certain problems, like 3-SAT and matching in specific graphs, at a significant time cost.

Second, any function taking n boolean inputs and producing a single bit of output, where the size of the mapping is k, can be realized using basic operations including a constant number of large OR, AND, and NOT gates, and their use shows a more efficient algorithm for at least one 3-SAT instance, showing a time complexity of O(n log^2.615555555555555555

Co-training is a semi-supervised learning technique that enables accurate predictions in specific domains without requiring extensive labeled data for training.
Recent research has demonstrated the effectiveness of co-training in various domain-specific tasks, particularly in session-based recommendation systems.
The co-trained model combines the representations of two distinct sessions and selects the most informative item from one session to enhance the other session's model.
Nonetheless, current co-training models treat sessions as unstructured graphs, ignoring the inherent self-guided nature of user sessions.
To address this limitation, we have developed an approach called self-guided graph co-training, which incorporates the self-guided nature of user sessions.
The proposed method constructs a co-training model based on two session-oriented graph neural networks and employs a unique item as a self-guiding node to optimize the target session's user-item interactions.
Experimental results have demonstrated the superiority of self-guided graph co-training in terms of recall metrics and it has shown potential for application in real-world scenarios.

This research expands the concept of LCM (Least Common Multiple) from numbers to groups, and based on the outcomes, LCM and Group Reversible LCM codes can be defined and examined in detail with examples provided. Additionally, a systematic method for generating GRLC codes is also included in the study.

We've established a new method to obtain rational expressions by shaping networks of algebraic geometry, specifically by developing an integrated framework that combines combinatorial and geometric approaches at its core. This methodology enables us to obtain a universal formula for invariant differential shapes on a combinatorial complex built from isomorphism classes of networks, which reduces to well-known invariant differential forms on configuration spaces when consisting of Riemann spheres. Furthermore, these rational expressions can be finite iterated iterated integrals with well-defined values for any network, opening up a new approach to electrodynamics Feynman amplitudes. This new framework provides a novel understanding of Feynman graphs and their amplitudes, revealing that certain classes of Feynman graphs yield polylogarithmic expressions with identifiable logarithmic limits at various orders.

A question arises regarding how an object classifier extracts object characteristics.
Research indicates that there is a strong connection between performance and efficiency in neural networks.
However, the relationship between these factors and classifier architecture is not entirely clear, particularly whether classifier efficiency depends on the relevance of object characteristics or their separation across different dimensions.
This study employs category-orthogonal characteristics, which are strongly associated with object categories, to train recurrent neural networks for object classification, examining the influence of computational effciency and the use of characteristic separability.
The results reveal that optimal classifier performance, and thus optimal processing of object characteristics, occurs when combining category-orthogonal characteristics with computational efficiency in recurrent neural networks.
The experiment demonstrates, for the first time, the vital role of neural network efficiency for extracting object characteristics during learning, and shows that optimal processing occurs when combining this efficiency with characteristics that are strongly associated with object categories and separable across different categories.

We investigate how interactions affect the topological properties of a one-dimensional model system, specifically how a reduction in the point-gap index occurs when a specific condition is met within an associated Hermitian model. By carefully analyzing a related model with a known phase transition, we demonstrate that another condition is required to maintain the point-gap index in its reduced state within a broader class of non-Hermitian models.

Research into CDS has been conducted for a long time, which can be used to increase the channel count in OFDM systems without leading to spectral expansion or phase distortion. We propose a new type of CGDS, specifically the m-ary CGDS of order l with size n (denoted as l-ary CGDS of size n and order l), which comprises l sets of distinct sets, where each set has exactly n different symbols and each symbol appears the same number of times across the entire set. Our research focuses on creating novel l-ary CGDS of order 2 and size 4 using a zeugma method, which involves combining two specific types of structures known as difference families.

The analysis of the ATLAS and CMS experiments' data, specifically the 2012 dataset with a total luminance of 36.3 fb^-1 and 35.9 fb^-1, has led to precise measurements of the Higgs boson's properties. The masses of the Higgs boson were measured as 125.36 GeV and 125.31 GeV, respectively. These findings have enabled calculations of the signal strength modifiers for both the loop-induced and directly mediated Higgs boson productions. The standard model predictions were supported by the experiment's data in a statistically significant manner. The experiment's data have been used to set limits on new physics beyond the standard model in the off diagonal couplings of the Higgs boson.

The capacity to detect changes in remote sensing satellites is increasingly important for monitoring the growth of human settlements. Currently, change detection methods are limited by the requirement for pre and post images in a specific spectrum, which hinders their application to diverse satellite datasets. Our proposed approach overcomes this limitation by using a single image, analyzing it separately in each spectral band and combining the extracted features. The unsupervised deep convolutional autoencoder encodes band-specific data, while a linear combination decoder integrates the encoded features to reconstruct the multispectral image. The reconstruction is compared to the original image to evaluate the encoding and decoding performance. Our proposed method demonstrates superior performance in alteration recognition, achieving an accuracy of 80.46% and a processing time of 10.4 seconds on the RXS dataset.

In 1988, Pan and Shiu made a notable discovery by determining the smallest integers k for which the equation y^2 = c_1^2 +...+ c_k^2 has an infinite number of solutions. They found these integers for various values of n and n mod 4. This discovery has been refined by replacing the equation with its two-dimensional counterpart y^2 = x_1^2 +...+ x_k^2. The current work aims to demonstrate that the series of primes dividing at least one variable in this new equation is finite.

Quantum tunneling between oriented silicon molecules can be observed with a scanning tunneling microscope, but in a particular configuration, the behavior is complicated by the interaction between the molecules. This effect can be explained by a simple model based on the characteristics of the lower energy states of silicon's constituent pentagonal dodecahedra. Notably, the model also reveals a coupling between charge and spin that causes the spectral features to shift and split in an applied magnetic field, an observation supported by computational calculations.

Researchers in optimization technology frequently utilize innovative techniques from the field of optimization to improve various technologies and systems. As a result, various cutting-edge innovations have emerged, such as advances in artificial intelligence, robotics, and autonomous navigation systems. As it becomes more widely recognized, there is a growing need for a unified and comprehensive platform that enables researchers to quickly develop and deploy optimized solutions. To address this requirement, we have created a standardized, modular software package known as LibOPT. This framework allows researchers to efficiently prototype and integrate new optimization algorithms by providing seamless interoperability with existing technologies and systems. By facilitating seamless collaboration and knowledge exchange among researchers in different institutions, the LibOPT framework promotes the rapid development and deployment of advanced optimization techniques in real-world applications.

T. C. Brown's concept of uniform algebras is introduced, along with its relationship to finite fields, specifically showing that the algebras of multilinear polynomials over finite fields are the only finite field examples. We define and assess the transferability of algebraic structures across different finite fields, identifying linear and multilinear polynomials as the highest in this category. Additionally, a new measure, the distinct elements value, is proposed to evaluate the field-freeness of polynomials, with a new bound suggested by this concept.

The identity of non-commutative spacetime entities remains an open question. By applying the quantum rules for parallel transport in the spacetime quantum model, we're able to establish a rule for transporting and interacting between individual spacetime particles. From this baseline, we develop a framework for describing the unique states of multiple, distinct spacetime particles. Given that the spacetime particles under consideration are fermionic in nature, their states exhibit a characteristic 'all-or-none' characteristic, reflecting the fundamental principles of fermionic behavior.

Precise control of material defects is crucial for creating advanced technological diamonds from high-purity synthetic single-crystalline material. A new technique combining optical patterning and electrical measurement has been developed to visually map the diamond's internal defect structure. This technique, a modification of transient-electrical-mapping methods, utilizes two-photon absorption to create patterns of specific defects, which are then electrically stimulated and measured to produce 3D images of the absorption site. Initial experiments using this technique were done on patterns of metallic grains embedded within the diamond, and the resulting images matched the known grain shapes very accurately.

This paper focuses on developing a comprehensive framework for MISOGYNO, misogyny-related content, classification on social media in the Arab world. Misogyny, which stems from the belief that men dominate over women, has far-reaching negative effects on society. By leveraging a pre-trainedBERT model and a carefully curated dataset comprising 20,000 misogynistic tweets, our research successfully distinguishes between various types of misogynistic content in the Arab world, ultimately achieving high accuracy rates in a framework that combines a classifier and a pre-trained language model.

This study aims to derive the existence and uniqueness of the solution for fractional backward stochastic differential equations (FBSDEs), taking into account a time-varying generator under both $\mathbb{F}$ and its minimum binary enlargement $\mathbb{F}^{\circ}$. The solution exists over a fractional Brownian motion orbit $\beta(t)$. The existence of the solution is demonstrated by first solving the predictable projection $\mathbb{F}$ of the augmented process $\mathbb{F}^{\circ}Y_{t}$, and then deriving $Y_{t}$.

In the realm of autonomous systems, developing controllers that can function effectively in unpredictable and dynamic environments remains a significant challenge. We introduce a novel policy-learning controller that is both resilient and efficient, using a stochastic approach. By integrating elements from stochastic control theory, our controller ensures a level of guaranteed performance under specific levels of uncertainty, even when that uncertainty arises from modeling inaccuracies. We also develop a method to simplify complex probabilistic models and establish an upper limit on the resulting estimation errors. Our introduced resilience framework is demonstrated through successful applications in two demanding scenarios: controlling a mobile robot on an unknown map and managing a drone in an environment with randomly changing wind conditions.

This paper presents an integrated approach to addressing multiple computation tasks in a distributed environment with a single cache. A unified scheme is developed that combines caching and decentralized computation, utilizing a general code and requiring minimal side information to complete each task. This strategy significantly reduces the amount of side information needed per unit of computation. Notably, this scheme achieves optimal results when the cache size equals one file and approaches optimality at cache size ten. It also outperforms an existing method by Heo et al. in various scenarios while matching performance at specific cache sizes. Furthermore, examples are provided to demonstrate that the unified approach yields better results than treating caching and computation separately and combining them on a file-by-file basis.

The Scott compactness principle is a fundamental concept in domain theory and program analysis, often employed outside of lambda calculus. In this work, we demonstrate the validity of the compactness principle within the Scott continuous functions framework in univalent set theory. Furthermore, within the types and units of homotopy type theory, where continuous functions cannot be directly defined, individual properties are characterized by describing mappings from types to spaces with specific paths, which align with existing definitions in other set theories and type theories assuming appropriate assumptions.

Using a key identity involving Eisenstein series generated by holomorphic modular forms and specific non-holomorphic kernels at critical Eisenstein cone positions, we derive the Maass-Shimura differential operator output for these series at half the critical values. Assuming the holomorphic component of the resulting series equals zero, our approach provides an alternative method to derive a finite combination of operators that apply to the full Eisenstein series, thereby proving the completeness of the finite-dimensional space associated with the total Eisenstein representations attached to the simultaneous images under the finite combination of Hecke operators associated with square-free integers.

Mobile robots with articulated limbs face potential risks when interacting with humans in close proximity. To mitigate this issue, we aim to safely integrate the robot's limbs with human bodies across a wide range of movements. To achieve this, our proposed secure control system first uses a lightweight, fast model of the robot's configuration, obtained through a reinforcement learning technique, to calculate safe speed limits at various points. These limits are then applied to the robot's standard movement plan using a secure gain method based on its configuration, resulting in a secure control framework that can accommodate any desired movement plan. We validate our framework's effectiveness through a real-world implementation on a mobile robotic arm.

Text summarization via a non-extractive approach using sentence representations. The extraction method utilizes sentence positions in the source text, whereas the excerpt method selects representative sentences that capture the overall meaning of the summary. In contrast, our proposed extractive method aims to overcome this limitation by generating an excerpted summary that not only reflects the original text but also highlights its most significant aspects. To achieve this goal, we suggest using graph-based sentence selection in the source text. Specifically, our proposed algorithm involves constructing a graph where nodes represent sentences and edges signify the relationship between them. By analyzing the importance of each node, our proposed method can identify key sentences that should be included in the summary.

Researchers have developed an extensive set of nonlinear equations capable of describing interacting bosons. These equations offer multiple advantages over conventional methods, including an inherent non-negative energy spectrum, correct statistical distribution for interacting bosons. They also provide an accurate representation of key physical properties such as energy and sound speed in the condensate, which align with traditional mean-field theory expectations. Furthermore, the posited operator framework can be applied to a range of models, such as the non-interacting and weakly interacting Bose gases. By utilizing the Gross-Pitaevskii model for condensates with interacting bosons, researchers have demonstrated that the posited nonlinear Schrödinger equation yields a non-negative energy spectrum and an exact match for the condensate's energy. Additionally, the method's applicability has been shown for higher levels of interaction, including the Lee-Huang-Yang model for bosons with low-level interactions.

Consider a complete K\"{a}hler manifold X and a projective variety X' in another projective variety X with hyperplane sections D_1 through d+1 that are distinct. If a meromorphic map f from X to X' avoids pole problems along a divisor with positive relative intersection, then it follows that if the pullbacks of these sections have maximal relative transcendence degree, the image of f covers all of X'. This result holds under two conditions: either the characteristic of the ground field is zero, or the characteristic is positive and the map f is morphism when restricted to a generic fiber of a holomorphic submersion from X to a base manifold B with relative ample image. This confirms a long-standing conjecture by Cartan and a related theorem from [Li, C. and X., F. (2019)] under the condition that X is a vector space and the map f is a meromorphic map rather than a morphism.

The core objective of our proposed signature-based method is to determine the non-degenerate component of the real part of an algebraic variety, defined by a polynomial system. We initially derive a novel expression for a signature polynomial set in terms of a polynomial system's image matrix, followed by analyzing its image to obtain the nondegenerate region. Using an established algorithm, we then calculate this nondegenerate region for a given polynomial system as a union of zero-level stratifications of specific points. We demonstrate the method's effectiveness and ease of implementation through examples implemented using MATLAB and SINGULAR.

In 2009, the STAR collaboration at the Brookhaven National Laboratory published their findings on "immediate photons" emitted during high-energy collisions between gold nuclei. These photons, which have very low energies, were found to originate from the interaction and provided valuable insight into the initial conditions of the collision. Although the physical characteristics of these photons have been studied using various methods, one key aspect that remains unclear is the direct contribution they make to the overall photon yield. A recent simulation using a specific model, the Landau and Tsallis model, accurately reproduced the overall photon spectrum, suggesting that these photons are a significant component of the overall yield, particularly at very low energies. This new assessment confirms that these photons are indeed a significant part of the overall photon yield in these types of collisions.

In 1989, Graham and Moxley addressed the Graham-Pollak theorem's multicolor variant by determining the minimum number of colored hyperplanes needed to cover all complete unit-length connections in a complete graph. Specifically, they found the minimum number of colored triangles in a complete graph with n vertices. However, the exact maximum number of unit-length tetrahedra in an n-vertex complete graph remains uncertain, which would lead to the resolution of the Graham-Pollak multicolor problem. This work presents initial steps in this endeavor by presenting upper and lower bounds for both the average and extreme cases of unit-length tetrahedra in n-vertex complete graphs.

Vector maps rendered using line connections can suffer from spatial aliasing when displayed at lower resolution than native. This issue arises due to low-resolution rendering producing a visually distorted version of the original high-resolution image. A novel, innovative approach has been developed to eliminate spatial aliasing in line-rendered vector maps, replacing traditional methods effective for raster images. This new technique not only maintains the inherent advantages of vector images, such as infinite scalability and zero file size, but also significantly reduces file sizes while preserving these benefits. Experimental results validate the effectiveness of this proposed method in achieving a aliasing-free rendering of line-rendered vector maps.

A novel infinite exponential function is proposed in the paper, which overcomes limitations of polynomial and rational functions while maintaining benefits of their respective forms. A corresponding quasi-interpolation scheme using this function is then developed and its properties analyzed in detail. Numerical examples provided in the study demonstrate the proposed interpolation method's efficacy in the computed domain compared to other techniques.

High-energy positrons from gamma-ray Pulsar shells are a key source to consider in searches for signs of Beyond the Standard Model new physics. We have carried out the most comprehensive study to date of the gamma-ray shell morphology of 48 nearby pulsars across the energy spectrum from 0.1 to 10 TeV. By combining the latest Fermi-LAT data with gamma-ray observations from HESS, MAGIC, and HESS, we have identified 18 pulsar shells that have been confirmed or strongly suggested. These include notable discoveries such as the confirmed shell of the Cas A remnant and the M28 shell, as well as the M101 shell which shows an unusual flat spectral shape. Our analysis has also revealed several previously unexplored pulsar remnants, and we have found that the spatial and energetic distribution of these objects exhibits unique characteristics. We have further evaluated the potential of upcoming observations from the CHERENKOV Fermi telescope and the IceCube lab to detect more gamma-ray emitting pulsar shells.

This research paper introduces a new dataset known as ClimateSonic, which is designed to classify climates according to the T\u00e9nory and \u00c9gler climate classification system. To expand the ClimateSonic dataset, a data augmentation technique was applied, resulting in a size of 30,000 images. To evaluate different T\u00e9nory and \u0xc3\x89gler climate classification methods, the paper conducts comprehensive experiments. A key finding of the study is that a novel approach outperforms existing methods by integrating a two-stage process involving an initial broad classification followed by a more detailed identification of the specific climate type. This approach surpassed the current state-of-the-art on the T\u00e9nory and \u0xc3\x89gler climate classification benchmark, ImageClimate10, achieving a test accuracy of 78.5%.

To bridge the gap between scientific climate research and public perception,
we examine societal norms regarding climate change through a social norms analysis.
This involves investigating the influence of climate researchers' societal views on
their own climate change stance and the relationship between their concerns about
climate norms and their own behavioral changes. Our study utilizes comprehensive survey
data from 472 German and 395 US climate researchers to provide insights into these views
and their regional variations. Additionally, we interact these norms with economic factors,
such as funding sources, to explore how supporting structures can promote societal
change through the climate research community. Our research offers policymakers and
decision-makers in the climate field useful indicators for effective communication strategies
and the promotion of climate research outcomes that society broadly accepts.

A novel approach utilizing the Koopman operator is presented for real-time modeling and regulation of soft multi-fingered grippers, offering an efficient linear representation of this complex, nonlinear system. By applying the method, a simplified and transferable model can be established, enabling efficient control implementation, design of observers for unmeasurable states, and analysis of its stability. Furthermore, the proposed strategy is validated experimentally, demonstrating its effectiveness in handling the complex dynamics of soft robotic grippers.

The Organic Generalized Residual Gradient Descent (OGRGD) is an advanced algorithm that seamlessly integrates Multi-Parameter Optimization (MPO) and Multi-Objective Optimization (MOO) methodologies to drive molecular design processes. Our work extends OGRGD by introducing a general formulation that allows for the use of any organic solver and any geometric distance function. In particular, we introduce the metric-based OGRGD ($\mathbf{g}$OGRGD}), which utilizes 3D geometric distances to define an objective space. To validate the algorithm's efficacy, we conducted experiments using end-to-end molecular design systems based on $\mathbf{g}$OGRGD, featuring three- and four-objective properties. The application of $\mathbf{g}$OGRGD was demonstrated with both Euclidean and Wasserstein-3 distances in our tests.

High-redshift young radio galaxies provide significant insights into the early stages of radio activity. The goal of this research is to establish a high-z young radio galaxy at a significantly distant location. A particularly striking radio source, designated J2102+6015, was recently discovered in the FAST survey. It is situated far away in space, approximately 4.575 billion light-years away. This powerful object has a significant luminosity, radiating 10^40.5 Watts per square metre. Using comprehensive multi-wavelength analysis combining data from various space telescopes like Chandra, XMM-Newton, and the NuSTAR, combined with ground-based facilities including VLT and GTC, we have obtained a detailed picture of J2102+6015. This research reveals that the source is composed of two compact active black hole sources, both situated within a small spatial distance of each other. This research provides the highest redshift record for a young radio galaxy, expanding our understanding of these powerful cosmic objects.

A new method is proposed to enhance the accuracy of predicting Non-small cell
Lung Cancer (NSCLC) subtypes by employing a more comprehensive approach that
involves additional sub-type related characteristics. Current sub-type prediction
models primarily rely on a limited set of features which may not be sufficient to
distinguish between sub-types effectively. To address this, a new framework
utilizes a multi-objective deep learning architecture to extract both traditional
and complex image characteristics from medical images. The framework then leverages
a Multi-dimensional Attention Mechanism (MAM) to identify and prioritize the
most influential features for sub-type prediction. Furthermore, a Multilabel
Neural Network (MLNN) is used to interpret the importance of various features in
relation to sub-type sub-classifications. The proposed method is evaluated on the
publicly available dataset and demonstrates superior performance with an improved
AUC score of 0.935 compared to the state-of-the-art methods.

In reinforcement learning, designing the system state requires input from domain experts. This process typically involves creating a list of states along with a description of each state's characteristics, which we refer to as natural language state descriptions. These descriptions enable domain users to annotate transitions relevant to the learning system by identifying their start and end states manually. However, experts may provide inaccurate descriptions due to potential ambiguities, and overly complex descriptions can hinder learning. Ultimately, these issues can lead to subpar interaction policy performance. This work aims to address these challenges by exploring methods to detect state confusion, annotate state transitions using more efficient techniques, and extract state features automatically using neural networks, based on these descriptions in a neural language model encoder framework.

A novel approach based on machine intelligence is proposed to reconstruct the cosmic energy spectrum, offering an alternative to the conventional assumption of an early cosmic energy density proportionality to temperature. Our computational model utilizes machine learning techniques, leveraging a comprehensive dataset of high-redshift quasars, to reconstruct the cosmic energy spectrum, corroborating its consistency with existing cosmological models and general relativity principles through a low root-mean-square error.

This study delves into certain subalgems derived from the Kac-Friedman Lie algems, specifically those related to polynomial rings over complex numbers, and systematically identifies and examines various types of module structures, namely primary, injective hulls of primary modules, and a subset of homogenous modules, proving they are inherently non-spindly. In addition, it also investigates the classification of spin modules within the local module category, establishing criteria for both complete and partial classifications under different conditions related to module composition lengths and degrees of module elements.

Over the last two decades, online sentiment analysis on social media platforms has become increasingly vital. With the exponential growth of data, traditional methods are shown to become increasingly cumbersome, prompting researchers to explore alternative solutions. Leveraging advanced deep learning models like Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks has become a popular approach in processing sequential data. This research paper outlines a complete LSTM-based framework for analyzing Twitter sentiment towards significant global events such as Olympics games. The proposed model was tested on two publicly available datasets, demonstrating superior performance compared to conventional sentiment analysis methods. The results show that LSTM networks can effectively utilize the information contained in social media posts, outperforming traditional techniques in assessing public opinion on major global events.

Conversational agents capable of engaging in casual dialogue have been extensively researched in the past.
However, the development of agents with more naturalistic conversations, capable of responding to unexpected inputs and unforeseen topics, remains an outstanding challenge.
To overcome this obstacle, we suggest an innovative approach that incorporates predefined character traits within a conversational framework.
This method is particularly effective when combined with large-scale language models, and we showcase a successful dialogue between a user and the system, featuring character 'Hermione Granger' from the Harry Potter series.
To realize this objective, we utilize an open-source dialogue system 'DialogFlow', extend its capabilities with large-scale language models 'BERT' and 'GPT2', and train these models on extensive datasets 'WikiText19' and 'WikiText20', 'Charity' and 'WikiText931'.
To give the system its unique personality, we use 'WikiText103' to fine-tune 'GPT2-LG' on various inputs including web pages about 'Hermione Granger', online forums 'Reddit', and conversational datasets 'CommonDialogue' and 'Multiwartz'.
Our ultimate goal is to achieve outstanding results with 'Hermione Granger', utilizing 'WikiText103' in conjunction with 'Charity' and 'WikiText931' for an open-domain conversation.

Usually, the concept of a gravitational wave backdrop refers to the collective effect 
of numerous sources emitting gravitational waves. However, the concept of "remembrance" 
suggests that a single source can also create a gravitational wave backdrop for another observer. 
This phenomenon can be best understood through the lens of a Schwarzschild black hole, 
where the gravitational waves produced by its collapse create a backdrop for a subsequent 
observer. The characteristics of these gravitational waves are distinct for different frequencies. 
At higher frequencies, the waves resemble those typically emitted by binary mergers, 
while at lower frequencies, they resemble stochastic processes. Research has already 
explored a scenario in which an advanced civilization attempts to decode the information 
contained within the waves of a previous gravitational wave event. This building block 
provides the foundation for a more comprehensive analysis of primitive and advanced 
civilizations interacting with gravitational waves.

We suggest that supergravity in early universe phase transitions could create large, temporary regions with high energy, resulting in a significant peak of high-energy neutrinos and emitting gravitational waves. These areas, linked to supersymmetry breaking, form during certain phase transitions, potentially creating high-energy events from the decay of these regions, attached to first-order transitions. High energy and frequency gravitational waves could be produced by the bubbles expanding during these transitions, resulting in significant signals from the regions themselves. As a result, high energy neutrinos and gravitational waves are created, offering a potential explanation for observed data, such as the potential Neutrino Telescope with Cubic Instruments (NTWCI) signals and gravitational waves from sources like the High Frequency Atomic Clocks (HFACs).

The development of a comprehensive theory of intelligence is impeded by our limited comprehension of natural language itself, let alone more abstract forms of communication.  Artificial General Intelligence models are particularly disadvantaged in scenarios involving communication between agents with limited shared information.  To overcome this limitation, we combine recent breakthroughs in neural machine translation and symbolic causal inference to design a neuro-symbolic signaling game that enables agents to learn and exchange higher-level semantic concepts, thereby generating a cohesive communication system.  The proposed approach enables agents to learn a shared semantic framework and effectively communicate complex ideas, resulting in increased cooperation and collaboration.

Predicting emerging terms within a social media environment is crucial for maintaining current knowledge and keeping with the times. For example, certain words may not be widely recognized at first but gain popularity over time, such as "Twitter" or "COVID". To effectively identify potential new terms, a hybrid framework is proposed that combines supervised learning from labeled data and unsupervised learning from unmarked social media posts. This framework uses a variety of statistical measures to pinpoint phrases that could be emerging terms and then evaluates their potential using learned patterns from previously successful new terms. The proposed method is evaluated using the Twitter dataset and compared to other approaches, demonstrating superior performance in several performance metrics.

E-commerce suggestions have become a crucial tool for assisting customers with session-based sessions-based conversations that consist of multiple interactions. Most current session-based recommendation models produce suggestions one item at a time, which can be time-consuming for customers. However, a session may include multiple potential suggestions that could Satisfy the customer's ultimate goal. By providing a ranking of these suggestions, we can improve the efficiency of the recommendation process and provide more relevant options sooner. To achieve this, our model employs a dual-head architecture that uses a customized loss function to simultaneously rank suggestions and Satisfy the click prediction task. By using rank representation for items, we can enhance the accuracy of our model's click predictions and ultimately provide better recommendations.

The movement of microscopic particles that self-generate activity within an environment that varies in activity levels has not been thoroughly examined experimentally. A study presented here investigates the behavior of a large particle that fits the criteria of a active colloid, which exists within a solution varying in activity levels. Over time, the particle moves from areas of low activity to areas of high activity, as evidenced by simulations based on a well-developed model. However, its forward and backward movement distances are unequal, resulting in a net movement toward areas of high activity levels. This net movement observed in the study agrees with the predictions made by the generalized Lowe-Capilar model.

However, traditional methods struggle with accurately capturing fracture complexity. A four-node tetrahedral network is used to discretize the domain, where the network's constitutive elements accurately capture the DFN geometry. A 19-cell element tetrahedron is used to discretize a single fracture element, with side faces used to represent fracture surfaces, and other elements (nodes, fracture edges, fracture corners) used for additional attributes.
